name: restic-backend-integrity-evidence
instr:
restic cannot use trustworthy, object-bound backend evidence to verify encrypted objects without unnecessary downloads. Add this support, using established full-content verification when evidence cannot prove the expected object and treating contradictions as corruption.

Define `IntegrityAlgorithm` in `internal/backend`: `IntegrityAlgorithmUnknown` (iota), `IntegrityAlgorithmMD5`, `IntegrityAlgorithmSHA1`, and `IntegrityAlgorithmSHA256`. Define `EvidenceScope`: `EvidenceScopeUnknown` (iota), `EvidenceScopeStoredObject`, and `EvidenceScopePayload`. Evidence must be deterministic and handle-bound. Reject malformed digests, impossible sizes, wrong objects, and incompatible scopes with `IntegrityEvidenceError`.

Define `VerificationDecision` in `internal/repository`: `VerificationUseEvidence` (iota), `VerificationReadBytes`, and `VerificationReject`. Define `VerificationMethod` with `VerificationMethodEvidence` (iota) and `VerificationMethodContent`. Strong matching evidence proves an object. Absent or insufficient evidence requires complete byte verification; conflicts mean corruption.

Backends from `azure.Create`, `b2.Create`, `gs.Create`, and existing local, REST, GS, memory, mock, and dry-run constructors expose evidence only for the selected visible stored object. Azure blob properties qualify only for the full object, never multipart composition metadata or ineligible properties. B2 uses SHA-1 from the selected visible version, never hidden or mismatched versions. Retry,
